title: Can I MASTER Chaturanga?
summary: Player plays chess.com Chaturanga (ancient chess) online vs ~1500 humans at 1-minute/bullet, goal 5 wins, and achieves it (wins game five). He finds the elephants weak and the game slow; learns the bare-king rule in game 5.
rules: Elephant (bishop slot): jumps exactly 2 squares diagonally (can leap over the middle square); reaches only 8 squares in total.
Chariot = rook; horse = knight; king = king.

Pawns move only 1 square forward (no double step, no en passant), capture diagonally; promotion happens automatically (to counselor/ferz, inferred from 'it automat...' and chess.com Chaturanga rules).
Bare-piece rule: a side that loses all its pieces except the king loses.
Stalemate: chess.com rule (inferred: stalemate counts as a loss for the stalemated side per chess.com Chaturanga) — transcript only says to avoid stalemate.
win_condition: Checkmate or bare the enemy king (capture all its other pieces).

opponent.name: online human opponents (chess.com Variants)
opponent.avatar_description: generic chess.com user avatar; random human usernames

setup: rnbkqbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w - - 0 1 with B=elephant, Q=counselor (white K on e1, counselor d1; black mirrors per chess.com, inferred).
